dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ami mi hoore na, yee am ɗum tawɗe njiɗɗoɗo sellal.
dialogue.translation: I agree, but we need to recognize each other's points clearly.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Maaɗa, wona deftere maɗa mawni ñalal wonaa fotti.
dialogue.translation: Indeed, then our journal of thoughts may not seem to reflect the truth.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mi teddere na, hokku ɗon yimɓe maɗa wonaa yee.
dialogue.translation: I differ, because the reasons from your side are not conclusive.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ami mi foddi no, mi ɗon yimɓe ɗum yee mi tawɗe naɗa.
dialogue.translation: I think so, and from your reasons, I agree with you.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Selli, mi hoore fotti naɗa, yee mi yeeɗi no sellal.
dialogue.translation: Clearly, I seem to agree with you, but I still have doubts.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Mi wonaa hokku ɗon miɗo, miɗo foddi naɗa sellal.
dialogue.translation: Then, the reason is from me, I think so distinctly.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ami mi teddere na, yee miɗo tawɗe naɗa ɗum.
dialogue.translation: I differ, but I admit your point among us.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Wona, miɗo hoore no sellal, yee ñalal wonaa wadata.
dialogue.translation: Then, we agree clearly, but the truth isn't settled.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Selli, mi foddi no, miɗoɗo foddi sellal.
dialogue.translation: Clearly, I think, we both think distinctly.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Amɗe, ko jom haa ɓeytin ɗun lekkere? Toobbintaa lekkere ɗon ɓalɗe.
dialogue.translation: Now, is the reason why even expressing an opinion offends? Protecting others from offense is important.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aa, meere ɗun ɗam. Hokkere haa lekkere ɓalɗe ɗen, ɗun wuro haa heɗɗaa lekkere.
dialogue.translation: Yes, it’s a matter that lasts. Forbidding offense within a group is difficult, and even in towns, it can still happen.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ko, amɗe lekkere haa heɗɗaa tobbinɗe ɓalɗe? Nden, jokkere haa heɗaa ɗon lekkere.
dialogue.translation: So, is offense allowed if it protects a group? No, disagreement is what helps prevent offense.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yii, lekkere haa heɗɗaa ɗon ɓalɗe, ɗun tobbinɗe tobbinɗe haa heɗɗaa.
dialogue.translation: Well, offense is allowed for a group, and protection is also allowed to happen.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Nden, ko meere ɗen haa heɗɗaa tobbinɗe haa heɗɗaa?
dialogue.translation: Then, is there any matter that should be protected to this extent?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aa, ɓeytinɗe koɗo haa heɗɗaa tobbinɗe. Nden, lekkere haa haɗaa tobbinɗe.
dialogue.translation: Yes, some opinions should be protected. Then, offense harms protection.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yii, meeɗo lekkere haa haɗaa tobbinɗe, ɗun hokkere haa heɗɗaa lekkere.
dialogue.translation: Well, if offense harms protection, then forbidding offense is also allowed.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ko, tobbinɗe ɓalɗe haa heɗɗaa lekkere. Nden, tobbinɗe tobbinɗe haa heɗɗaa.
dialogue.translation: So, protecting a group from offense is allowed. And protection should continue.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Aa, tobbintaa lekkere ɗon haa tobbinɗe haa heɗɗaa.
dialogue.translation: Yes, protecting others from offense is what should be allowed to happen.

key_phrases.phrase: Meere ɗun ɗam.

key_phrases.phrase: Lekkere haa heɗɗaa tobbinɗe ɓalɗe.
key_phrases.translation: Offense is allowed to protect a group.

key_phrases.phrase: Hokkere haa heɗɗaa lekkere.
key_phrases.translation: Forbidding offense is allowed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hunnduko ɓalɗo ɗaɗ, sawru rewɓe ɓeyyɗo, ɓurɗe ɗaɗ ko ɓeyyɗo wonnde.
dialogue.translation: According to injustice, even wealth must be curbed, opportunity must exist as long as equity is the rule.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aa, mi wonno dabare ɓurɗe nder yimɓe ɗum. Niɗin nder sawru nder ɓeyyɗo.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I understand the basis of the system in our society. It lies in wealth and opportunity.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ko ɗaɗe ɓalɗe nder ɓurɗe, sawru ɗaɗ rewɗe ɓeyyɗo.
dialogue.translation: But as long as injustice persists in the system, wealth does not restore opportunity.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Te mi han feereɗo ɓalɗo, ɓeyyɗo ɗaɗ wonnde nder ɓurɗe.
dialogue.translation: Yet I think injustice can be reduced provided equity exists in the system.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hunnduko ɓalɗo, ɓeyyɗo nder sawru ɗaɗ rewɗe dabare.
dialogue.translation: According to injustice, opportunity in wealth only restores the basis.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aa, mi ƴaamaɗo ko ɓalɗo ɓurɗe wonaɗa ko ɓeyyɗo, ɗaɗ hunnduko wonnde.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I believe that injustice in the system is not just about opportunity, but about equity.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ko mi renɗe dabare nder sawru, ɓeyyɗo ɗaɗ rewɗe ɓalɗo.
dialogue.translation: But I explain the basis in wealth: opportunity restores injustice.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ɗaɗ hunnduko wonnde, sawru ɗaɗ rewɗe ɓeyyɗo, ko ɓalɗo ɓurɗe wonaɗa.
dialogue.translation: As long as equity exists, wealth restores opportunity, not injustice in the system.

key_phrases.phrase: Hunnduko ɓalɗo, sawru rewɓe ɓeyyɗo, ɓurɗe ɗaɗ ko ɓeyyɗo wonnde.
key_phrases.translation: According to injustice, wealth must be curbed, opportunity must exist as long as equity is the rule.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mi wattitudo, ɗum ɓurɗo ɓeyyɗo ɓeytin keewa aɗa tolla rewɗe ɗokkere kala.
dialogue.translation: I wonder, whether our decisions about genetic engineering truly lead to consequences we can control.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Mun yettinɗe keewa aɗa teddere ɓurɗo ɗoree ɗum hollit.
dialogue.translation: But isn’t it that every choice we make carries precisely a risk?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ɓeytin ɗum, ɓeyyɗo tolaa ɗokkere ɗum ɗunɗunɗe ƴamɗu.
dialogue.translation: Our responsibility is to ensure that our methods are balanced.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hollit ɓeyyɗo teddere keewa aɗa gollinde ƴamɗu.
dialogue.translation: Risk is always present if we act without caution.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mi wattitudo ɗunɗunɗe ƴamɗu keewa aɗa wona ɓeyyɗo tan.
dialogue.translation: I wonder if we are truly capable of ensuring safety.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ɗokkere ɗum teddere ɓurɗo keewa tawɗe teddere ɓeytin teddere.
dialogue.translation: Our methods must always consider every decision and every responsibility.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mi keewa aɗa hollit teddere ƴamɗu, ɓeytin teddere ƴamɗu.
dialogue.translation: I think that if risk is always present, so is responsibility.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Mi ƴamɗu keewa aɗa ɓurɗo teddere ƴamɗu keewa aɗa ɓeyyɗo teddere.
dialogue.translation: I believe that every choice carries a responsibility and an ability.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mi wonaa keewa aɗa a tawɗe tan ƴamɗu ɓeytin tan.
dialogue.translation: I’m not sure if this alone is enough for responsibility.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɓeytal ɓeɗɗe muɓɗa danye, ɓeytino ɗaaɗiɗo anndiiɗo nguɓɗo. Muɗum nafataa nafatugol ɗum ɗaaɗiɗo.
dialogue.translation: Change is inevitable in life, and transformation guides our understanding. It needs that guidance to be effective.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ɓeydude ɓurɗo mbɗeɗo ɗaaɗo, hokku ɗaaɗo wonaa ko ɓeytal. Anndiiɗo maayɗo wonaa ko nafatugol.
dialogue.translation: We cannot afford to lose the strength of tradition, no matter how new the change is. Knowledge from the past is not just a need.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Muɗum ɓurɗude ɗaaɗo, hokku ɗaaɗo wonaa ko ɗaaɗiɗo. Ko mbɗeɗo ɗaaɗo, anndiiɗo maayɗo ɓeytino.
dialogue.translation: It is this empowerment of the new that does not negate guidance. Even if the new is strong, ancestral knowledge remains transformative.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ɓeytal ɗaaɗo, muɗum nafataa nafatugol ɗum ɗaaɗiɗo. Anndiiɗo maayɗo wonaa ko ɓeyduno ɓurɗo.
dialogue.translation: Change is new, and it needs that guidance to be effective. The knowledge of the past is not a waste of strength.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɓurɗo ɗaaɗo nafataa ɗaaɗiɗo. Muɗum ɓurɗude ɗaaɗo, hokku ɓurɗo wonaa ko nafatugol.
dialogue.translation: The strength of the new needs guidance. This empowerment of the new does not mean the power of tradition is a mere necessity.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hokku ɗaaɗo, anndiiɗo maayɗo wonaa ko ɓeytino. Muɗum nafataa nafatugol ɗum ɗaaɗiɗo.
dialogue.translation: Despite the newness, the knowledge of the past remains transformative. It still needs that guidance to be effective.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɓurɗo ɗaaɗo, ɓurɗo maayɗo, hokku nafataa nafatugol ɗaaɗiɗo. Ko mbɗeɗo ɓurɗo, anndiiɗo wonaa ko ɓeytal.
dialogue.translation: The new strength, the old strength—both need that guidance to be effective. Even if strength is strong, knowledge does not remain static.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hokku ɓeyduno, muɗum nafataa nafatugol ɗaaɗiɗo. Anndiiɗo maayɗo wonaa ko ɓurɗo ɗaaɗo.
dialogue.translation: Without loss, it still needs that guidance to be effective. The knowledge of the past is not the same as the power of the new.

dialogue.text: Na'i, ɗum leɓɓe ɓuri wannge faam foon na'i ɓeyyi maayɗo.
dialogue.translation: Lawyer, only the laws need to change so that lawyers understand them better.

dialogue.text: Mi na'i, ɗof đuɗɗaaɗi baaɗi wannge, ɓeyyi faam taaɗi hakkunde leɓɓe.
dialogue.translation: I, as a lawyer, believe some rules must change, so they can be better understood under the law.

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.text: Na'i, mi ɗemngal leɓɓe taaɗi, foon no faam foon no wannge wadde maayɗoɓe.

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ɓeyyi leɓɓe wannge, foon no faam, foon no na'i ɓeyyi maayɗoɓe.
dialogue.translation: Better change the laws so that people understand, so lawyers help everyone.

scenario: Exploring the relationship between language and thought
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Pulaar

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Fool ɗum ɗee hakkunde hokkere ɗon jokkere taalugol?
dialogue.translation: Does thinking solely depend on the ideas behind language?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Haa, foolɗam ɓere gooto taalugol soowtaa. Tawa foolɗo jomɗo na'i.
dialogue.translation: Yes, our thinking shapes language in a certain way. Thus, thought guides speech.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hokkere ɗum jokkere gooto taalugol, tawa wadii foonɗo toow.
dialogue.translation: Some concepts in language limit what we can think, isn’t it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Wadii foonɗo toowɗo. Tawa taalugol soowtaa ɗon hokkereɗen.
dialogue.translation: Yes, it limits our thought. Language shapes our ideas in return.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Foolɗo nokkuɗo gooto hokkereɗen walɗeɗo gooto taalugol.
dialogue.translation: Our thoughts reflect certain ideas, which in turn reflect language.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Haa. Wadii foolɗo gooto taalugol, tawa soowtaa hokkereɗen ɗon foonɗo.
dialogue.translation: Yes. While thought shapes language, it also forms ideas about thought.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hokkereɗen walɗeɗo gooto foolɗo, tawa ɗaaɗo jomɗo na'i.
dialogue.translation: Ideas reflect thought, but thought also guides speech.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Tawa, foonɗo mawndeɗo gooto taalugol foonɗo toow.
dialogue.translation: Thus, our minds are shaped by the language we use.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Haa, foolɗo soowtaa taalugol, tawa taalugol soowtaa foolɗo. Tawa soɗdeɗo gooto wuro.
dialogue.translation: Yes, thought shapes language, and language shapes thought. That’s why there’s a connection.

dialogue.text: Hoowaa seewta mbadde ɗiɗi? Wule ndima gooto yimɓe yiɗde ɗum fewre.
dialogue.translation: Why do you allow danger to persist like this? A direct action could bring more benefit to everyone.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Nden, ndima wule ɗon rewɓe ɓeydo hokku laamu. Sewta kay joodi.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Nden, wule ndima ɗanɗanɗoo kay suuɗi. Mbimbi kay suuɗi kay hoowaa sewta.
dialogue.translation: But direct action isn’t always safe. A safe community doesn’t always allow danger.

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Kanɗo mbeɗɗi yimɓe ɗimmal ɓeŋɗe ɗonɗe, ko heewa ndiyam koɓɓe deftere?
dialogue.translation: Do you think that scientists truly understand the nature of reality, or is it precisely what they claim?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aa, miɗo ɓeɗiɓe ɗeɗe ɗumɗu hoɗɗu ɓeydo laamu ɓeŋɗe. ɓeɗi wulɗe ɗaɗa, ɗumma haa laamu haɗaɗɗa.
dialogue.translation: Well, there are places where we try to push the limits of knowledge, but which remain out of reach. It's true, but some still exist beyond our grasp.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Nde maɓɓe ɗimmal ɗaɗa, ɓeɗiɓe ɗere hoɗɗu ɓeŋɗe ɗeɗe ɗumɗu ɓeydo wulɗe?
dialogue.translation: If that's the case, then new boundaries of knowledge will always be explored, no matter how far we try to go?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ɓeɗiɓe nden, ɗumɗu ɗaɗa ɗimmal ɓeŋɗe koɓɓe laamu ɗamɗam.
dialogue.translation: In some cases, we attempt to understand a matter which science knows only a little about.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Haa, maɓɓe ɗimmal ɗaɗa ɓeɗiɓe wulɗe ɗeɗe ɗumɗu, ɗum ɗimmal ɗaɗa koɓɓe deftere?
dialogue.translation: Yes, but if understanding is still limited in some places, can it ever be truly precise?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ɗaɗa, ɗumma ɗimmal ɗeɗe ɗumɗu ɓeydo wulɗe, ɓeɗiɓe ɗere hoɗɗu ɓeŋɗe ɗonɗe.
dialogue.translation: However, even where we try to grasp what's unknown, new boundaries of knowledge always emerge.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Koɓɓe maɓɓe hoɗɗu ɓeŋɗe ɗeɗe wulɗe, ɓeɗiɓe ɗimmal ɗaɓɓe deftere?
dialogue.translation: But if the limits of a matter are known, can understanding be truly exact?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aa, ɗeɗe ɗumma ɓeɗiɓe ɗimmal ɗaɗa, wulɗe hoɗɗu ɓeŋɗe ɗonɗe ɓeɗiɓe ɗere.
dialogue.translation: Well, in those places where understanding is still limited, the boundaries of knowledge remain, and new ones may appear.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Nde maɓɓe ɗimmal ɓeŋɗe koɓɓe deftere, ɓeɗiɓe hoɗɗu ɓeŋɗe nden?
dialogue.translation: So if understanding is precise about a matter, are there still limits to knowledge?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɓe toowti naaɗɗi ko ɗaaɗaa mbaɓɓe.
dialogue.translation: They really convinced me with that argument.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ɓeɗe mawɗo ɗum. Wotoore kaɓɓe toowtiɗe mbaddu?
dialogue.translation: What's more about it? Why did they persuade you specifically?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɗaaɗaa ɓuri ɓeɗe ɗaaɗaa tam yaltude nden dammugol.
dialogue.translation: Truly, the root of it is just logical consistency and evidence.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ɗen rewtiɗe ko ɓeydo haaɓe?
dialogue.translation: And did they repeat it according to their source?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɗum, rewtiɗe naaɗɗi ɗaaɗaa tawɗo.
dialogue.translation: Yes, they repeated it really well.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Haiɗo mawɗo ɓeɗe wotoore kaɓɓe toowtiɗe ndenɗe ɓeɗe ɓeɗe?
dialogue.translation: What else can we add to their arguments to strengthen them?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɓeɗe toowtaɗe ko ɗaaɗaa ko ɓiɗɓi ɗenɗe ko ɓuri.
dialogue.translation: The best way to convince is to use clear arguments and solid reasoning.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ndenɗe ko ɗeɗe ɓeɗeɗe wotoore ko haaɓe toowtaɗe?
dialogue.translation: And do concrete examples help in convincing?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɗaaɗaa, ko ɗeɗe ko haaɓe toowtaɗe tawɗo. Dammugol ɗeɗe ɓeɗe mawɗo ɓeɗeɗe.
dialogue.translation: Yes, concrete examples greatly help in convincing. Evidence strengthens arguments even more.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ndogaa ko won ɓidɗe ɓeydoɗo laamu, lula ɗum tunɓiɗo?
dialogue.translation: I wonder what the government decided to allow, even though we strongly oppose it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: A naɗa sata mbaa ɗum gooɗo faɗaɗa, ɗum kala walaa laamu.
dialogue.translation: The reason is so that this matter can proceed alone, without the government.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɓidɗe naɗa ko yaltudeɗo, ko gooɗo laamu?
dialogue.translation: Did they decide because of humanitarian reasons, or to advance the government's agenda?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Tam ɓe sebbal, ko won ɓidɗeɗo wonɗe, laamu gooɗo na sata naɗa.
dialogue.translation: Now I see, what they decided is what the government moves forward with as its reason.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɗum tunɓiɗo laamu non, ko sata ɓeɗiɗo naɗa gooɗo?
dialogue.translation: We oppose the government, but is there any valid reason for them to advance this?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: A sata kala naɗa, non ɓeɗɗo lula won ndimaɗo hoɗɗu.
dialogue.translation: The only reason is this, but there are also other ethical complications.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ko wonɗe ɓeydoɗo gooɗo, non ko wale laamuɗo?
dialogue.translation: What allows them to move forward, even against the people's will?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Mbaa laamuɗo ɓeydoɗo goo, non ko ɗumɗu laamu gooɗo faɗaɗa.
dialogue.translation: So that the government permits it to move, but only if this matter is beneficial.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Aɗa, ɓeɗɗo ndimaɗo non, ko ɓidɗeɗo naɗa ɓeɗɗo lula wonɗe goo.
dialogue.translation: Alright, but there are still ethical issues, and they decided this based on what suits them.

key_phrases.translation: I wonder what they decided...

key_phrases.translation: The reason is so that this matter can proceed...

key_phrases.translation: And they decided this based on what suits them.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɗaaɗeɓe ko ɓurnde ɓeydo mawɗo, ɓe koy wonaa neɗɗo ɓeɗɗo.
dialogue.translation: These works also reflect, according to the dominant language, what they truly claim.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aɗa timtim, ko ɓoy ɗum ɓeɗɗo ɓeɗɗon. ɓeɗɗo mawɗo ka ɓeydo ndima.
dialogue.translation: But gradually, the voices also give examples. The dominant examples shape the language.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɗeɓe koy neɗɗo ɓeɗɗo ko ɓeɗɗo mawɗo ɗaaɗeɓe.
dialogue.translation: They say that these examples, however, are the ones that truly reflect the dominant perspective.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Wonaa, ɗen ɗaaɗeɓe ɓurnde ɓeyɗo mawɗo kaɓɓe. Aɗa timtim, ɓoy ɗum ɗen.
dialogue.translation: Really, those reflections are according to the dominant language, but gradually the voices also.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Nden ko ɓeɗɗo mawɗo ɗaaɗeɓe ko ɓoy ɗum ɗeɓeɓe.
dialogue.translation: But those dominant examples reflect what their voices also express.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aɗa, ko ɓeɗɗo mawɗo kaɓɓe, ɓurnde ɓeyɗo kaɓɓe, ɓeɗɗo ndima.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but the dominant examples, according to the dominant language, shape the language itself.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Wonaa, ɓeɗɗo mawɗo ɗaaɗeɓe ko ɓoy ɗum kaɓɓe.
dialogue.translation: Really, the dominant examples reflect what the voices also shape.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Nden, aɗa timtim, ɓoy ɗumɗu kaɓɓe ndima.
dialogue.translation: But gradually, the voices too, slowly shape the language.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Haa, ɓeɗɗo mawɗo ɗaaɗeɓe ko ɓoy ɗum kaɓɓe ndima.
dialogue.translation: Yes, the dominant examples reflect what the voices also shape in the language.
